item.research_question: How can fatigue life be enhanced in high-entropy alloys at low strain amplitudes without sacrificing ductility, specifically by addressing the trade-off between fatigue strength and fatigue-crack-initiation resistance in precipitation-strengthened alloys?
item.material_system: Al0.5CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy containing an FCC matrix and multicomponent B2 precipitates (NiAl-type)
item.processing_route: Vacuum-induction melting to fabricate a large plate, followed by hot rolling with 60% reduction at 1150 °C, and annealing at 1000 °C for 1 h
item.test_conditions: Monotonic tension at RT with a strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; fully-reversed strain-controlled low-cycle fatigue (LCF) at RT with strain amplitudes from ±0.1% to ±1.75% and a strain rate of 1 × 10−2 s−1; real-time in situ neutron diffraction at strain amplitudes of ±0.5%, ±1%, and ±1.75%
key_findings: The alloy exhibits at least four times longer fatigue life than conventional alloys at a plastic strain amplitude of ~0.03%.
The B2 phase bears significantly more stress than the FCC phase after yielding, with lattice strains nearly ten times larger.
Stress-induced martensitic transformation (SIMT) occurs in the B2 phase, evidenced by abnormal peak broadening and peak separation in neutron diffraction.
Deformation twinning is observed in the FCC matrix only at high strain amplitudes (≥1.75%), not at intermediate amplitudes (1%).
The B2 phase is plastically deformable at all tested strain amplitudes, storing dislocations and relieving stress concentration.
Fine B2 precipitates act as efficient crack arresters, forming blunted cracks, whereas coarse band-like B2 precipitates initiate microcracks.
The multicomponent B2 phase has lower antiphase boundary (APB) energies (e.g., compared to 0.697 eV/m² for pure NiAl) enabling plastic deformation.
item.mechanism: The enhanced fatigue life is attributed to the ductile-transformable character of the multicomponent B2 precipitates, which undergo reversible martensitic transformation and plastic deformation to accommodate strain incompatibility with the FCC matrix. This mechanism relieves stress concentration at phase boundaries, retards microcrack initiation, and provides alternative deformation pathways, unlike brittle traditional intermetallics.
item.limitations: The study notes that if the B2 phase size is too large (e.g., band-like precipitates), it becomes easy to initiate microcracks due to longer incoherent interfaces where stress concentration cannot be effectively accommodated.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the design strategy of introducing ductile-transformable multicomponent intermetallic precipitates can guide the design of fatigue-resistant alloys by tuning HEA compositions and thermomechanical processing.
quotes: the current HEA shows at least four times longer life than conventional alloys
the B2 phase continuously bears more stress after yielding
